newsitem.title: philippines: Philippine peso ends unchanged in range trade.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends unchanged in range trade.

text.p: * Central Bank seen out of the market
The Philippine peso closed unchanged at 26.344 on Monday in range trading as banks marked their time waiting for a decision on U.S. interest rates, traders said.
The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee will meet on Tuesday.
"They don't want to be aggressively short on the dollar in case of a 0.25-percentage increase in the U.S. interest rate," a big bank dealer said.
The peso opened at 26.34 and later fell to 26.344 after the T-bill auction resulted in a lower 91-day T-bill rate of 9.724 from 9.804 percent.

"The market is cautious because domestic interest rates are going down. On the other hand, borrowing rates on the dollar are going up," one trader said. A lower interest rate premium of the peso will make it less attractive to hold.
But the peso was locked in a band because banks would like to have a lot of pesos for the long Easter holidays, traders said.
The day's average was at 26.342 from 26.339 as market volume fell to $98.0 million from $191.10 million.
